newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares sag on profit-taking, Fed in focus.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares sag on profit-taking, Fed in focus.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower on Monday in a basically positive market, hit by profit-taking and speculation on a possible Fed rate rise later in the week, with dealers seeing cautious days ahead.
"The market was optimistic to start with but profit-taking and fears of the consequences of a possible U.S. rate rise at the Fed's Tuesday meeting hit the market," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index closed 0.42 point lower at 144.36 in overall bourse turnover of 1.252 billion crowns. The KFX March future fell 0.10 point to 144.75 with 60 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
It was profit-taking in bank paper which was responsible for much of the decline. Den Danske Bank finished six crowns down at 492, while rival Unidanmark fell seven crowns to 351.

A.P. Moeller's D/S Svendborg also contributed to the general fall, closing 2,666 crowns lower at 255,000, while East Asiatic dropped four to 149 on a media warning by CEO Michael Fiorini not to entertain exaggerated expectations for the company.
ISS was the day's winner, with 630,000 shares changing hands to finish off 14 crowns up at 160 on positive media reaction to the sale of its troubled U.S. ISS Inc. unit.
